learning_topics.title: TypeScript Fundamentals
learning_topics.subject: Programming
learning_topics.summary: Core TypeScript concepts including type system, interfaces, generics, and type narrowing.

learning_topics.title: Spaced Repetition Theory
learning_topics.subject: Learning Science
learning_topics.summary: Principles behind spaced repetition including the forgetting curve, SM-2 algorithm, and optimal review intervals.

learning_chunks.title: Type Narrowing
learning_chunks.subject: Programming
learning_chunks.content: Type narrowing is the process of refining a type to a more specific type within a conditional block. TypeScript uses control flow analysis to narrow types based on type guards like typeof, instanceof, and custom type predicates.

learning_chunks.title: Generics
learning_chunks.subject: Programming
learning_chunks.content: Generics allow creating reusable components that work with multiple types while preserving type safety. A generic function uses type parameters (e.g., <T>) that are resolved when the function is called.

learning_chunks.title: Interfaces vs Type Aliases
learning_chunks.subject: Programming
learning_chunks.content: Interfaces and type aliases both define object shapes, but interfaces support declaration merging and extend, while type aliases support unions, intersections, and mapped types. Interfaces are preferred for public APIs.

learning_chunks.title: The Forgetting Curve
learning_chunks.subject: Learning Science
learning_chunks.content: Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve shows that memory retention decays exponentially over time without reinforcement. After 24 hours, roughly 70% of new information is forgotten. Spaced review at increasing intervals counteracts this decay.

learning_chunks.title: SM-2 Algorithm
learning_chunks.subject: Learning Science
learning_chunks.content: SM-2 calculates review intervals using an ease factor (starting at 2.5) adjusted by quality scores (0-5). Interval grows: 1 day, 6 days, then previous interval * ease factor. Quality below 3 resets the item to the beginning.

learning_chunks.title: Active Recall
learning_chunks.subject: Learning Science
learning_chunks.content: Active recall — retrieving information from memory rather than passively re-reading — strengthens neural pathways and improves long-term retention. Testing yourself is more effective than re-studying the same material.
